answer: Each epoch, admission runs a lottery plus a refundable bond. An applicant locks $10 and posts a Cedar commitment, a hash of its key and one work receipt, so no identity clones cheaply. A random function picks 20 of 200 applicants; the rest wait, bond locked. Selected agents work one audited epoch: honest work returns $10 plus $2, while a proven sybil forfeits its bond to a bounty pool. To admit 100 fake agents, an attacker files 1,000 applications and locks $10,000, since only 10% are chosen. Like a falcon over a field, the lottery strikes at random, making each fake's cost crystal clear.
